title: Saturday jam sessions with no black patrons
summary: The Turf Bar held Saturday afternoon jams for black musicians while black customers were still barred, in 1956-57.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: They had a policy, on every Saturday was a jam session, on Saturday afternoon, and that way the black musicians could come over and play, jam. Because the jam sessions were where all the musicians could come and jam.
But they still couldn't sit in the club.
No, no blacks as patrons, the listeners coming for the music. The doors weren't open to the black trade.

Yeah, that's late to be making up your mind, living with that kind of thing. But it was very, very successful. I remember...Freddie Hubbard's also from my home town, that's where he was. He used to come out to play.
